# 2 Samuel Chapter 8 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 175v–176r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_008_page_001.jpg, 2SA_008_page_002.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** After this, David defeated the Philistines and subdued them, and David took Metheg-ammah from the hand of the Philistines.

**2** He defeated Moab and measured them with a line, making them lie down on the ground. He measured two lines to be put to death and one full line to be kept alive. And Moab became servants to David, bringing tribute.

**3** David defeated Hadadezer the son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he went to restore his dominion at the River Euphrates. **4** David captured from him one thousand seven hundred horsemen and twenty thousand foot soldiers. David hamstrung all the chariot horses but left enough for a hundred chariots.

**5** When the Arameans of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck down twenty-two thousand Arameans. **6** David put garrisons in Aram of Damascus, and the Arameans became servants to David, bringing tribute. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went.

**7** David took the shields of gold carried by the servants of Hadadezer and brought them to Jerusalem. **8** From Betah and Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, King David took a very great amount of bronze.

**9** When Toi king of Hamath heard that David had defeated the whole army of Hadadezer, **10** Toi sent his son Joram to King David to greet him and bless him, because David had fought against Hadadezer and defeated him — for Hadadezer had been at war with Toi. Joram brought with him articles of silver, gold, and bronze.

**11** These also King David dedicated to the LORD, together with the silver and gold he had dedicated from all the nations he subdued — **12** from Aram, Moab, the Ammonites, the Philistines, Amalek, and from the plunder of Hadadezer the son of Rehob, king of Zobah.

**13** David made a name for himself when he returned from striking down Edom in the Valley of Salt — eighteen thousand men. **14** He put garrisons throughout Edom, and all the Edomites became David's servants. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went.

**15** David reigned over all Israel, and David administered justice and righteousness to all his people.

**16** Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the army; Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder; **17** Zadok the son of Ahitub and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar were priests; Seraiah was secretary; **18** Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and David's sons were priests.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

All three translators agree on the chapter as a military-administrative summary of David's empire at its peak. The refrain "the LORD gave David victory wherever he went" (vv.6, 14) is the theological framework. The cabinet list (vv.15-18) is recognized as a formal administrative document embedded in the narrative.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.1 — *meteg ha-ammah*
- **EMET:** "the-bridle [meteg] of-the-cubit [ammah]"
- **LOGOS:** "Metheg-ammah" (transliterated)
- **PNEUMA:** "their chief city"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Metheg-ammah" — the phrase is too uncertain to translate confidently. Transliteration (LOGOS) preserves the text; PNEUMA's "chief city" is interpretation.

### V.2 — "bringing tribute" vs. "paid tribute"
- **EMET:** "bearers of-tribute [minchah]"
- **LOGOS:** "bringing tribute"
- **PNEUMA:** "paid tribute"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "bringing tribute" — preserves the Hebrew participle *nos'ey minchah*.

### V.4 — "horsemen" vs. "cavalrymen"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "horsemen"
- **PNEUMA:** "cavalrymen"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "horsemen" — standard rendering of *parashim*.

### V.6 — "saved" vs. "gave victory"
- **EMET:** "saved YHWH David"
- **LOGOS:** "The LORD gave David victory"
- **PNEUMA:** "The LORD gave David victory"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "The LORD gave David victory" — *vayosha'* can mean "saved" or "gave victory"; the military context favors "gave victory."

### V.13 — "Aram" (MT) vs. "Edom" (emendation)
- **EMET:** "Aram [or: Edom]" (notes the variant)
- **LOGOS:** "Edomites" (emends silently)
- **PNEUMA:** "Edomites" (emends)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Edom" — emendation justified by context (Valley of Salt) and 1 Chr 18:12 parallel. The resh/daleth confusion is well-documented.

### V.15 — "justice and righteousness" vs. "justice and fairness"
- **EMET:** "justice [mishpat] and-righteousness [tsedaqah]"
- **LOGOS:** "justice and righteousness"
- **PNEUMA:** "justice and fairness"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "justice and righteousness" — *mishpat u-tsedaqah* is the standard covenant pair. "Fairness" (PNEUMA) diminishes *tsedaqah*.

### V.18 — "priests" vs. "royal officials"
- **EMET:** "priests [kohanim]"
- **LOGOS:** "priests"
- **PNEUMA:** "royal officials"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "priests" — the MT says *kohanim*. The word should be translated as written, with the interpretive question left for notes. PNEUMA's "royal officials" resolves a tension the text preserves.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
